exposure: Maternal ORF-B2L genetic vaccine (intramuscular injection of recombinant ORF-B2L DNA and a subunit protein)
outcome: Maternal and neonatal specific anti-B2L antibodies
Maternal and neonatal Th1 and Th2 cytokine levels
Placental transcriptomics (differentially expressed genes, immune cell recruitment, cytokine signalling, hormone regulation pathways)
Neonatal spleen transcriptomics (differentially expressed genes, T and B cell development, pathogen defence, Th1/Th2-biased immunity)
cohort: Pregnant female rats were given intramuscular injections of either a gene vaccine or an empty plasmid as a control.
finding: Maternal ORF-B2L genetic vaccination induces a robust immune response, enhancing maternal-foetal protection and shaping neonatal immune responses.
